new_entities.name: Neurofeedback for ADHD in children
aliases: portable EEG-based neurofeedback for childhood ADHD
new_entities.description: EEG-based neurofeedback training used in children or adolescents with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder.

new_entities.name: ADHD symptom severity
aliases: childhood ADHD inattention and hyperactivity severity
new_entities.description: Overall severity of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder symptoms measured by clinician, parent, teacher, or blinded rater scales.

edges.effect_quant: The most rigorous recent synthesis found no significant benefit on probably blinded ADHD total symptom ratings overall (SMD 0.04, 95% CI -0.10 to 0.18), although a smaller favorable signal emerged in standard-protocol subgroups and some newer portable EEG trials report between-group improvement.
edges.population: children and adolescents with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder treated with clinic-based or portable EEG neurofeedback protocols
edges.mechanism: Neurofeedback is meant to train self-regulation of cortical activity patterns linked to inattention and impulsivity. If learning transfers outside the training setting, symptoms could improve; if it does not, gains may mainly reflect expectancy, therapist attention, or rater proximity rather than durable core symptom change.
edges.summary: This edge should stay mixed rather than promotional. Some neurofeedback trials show symptom improvement, but the strongest blinded-outcome meta-analyses still find little or no clear benefit on core ADHD severity.
edges.caveats: Results are highly sensitive to rater blinding, protocol quality, and whether true neural self-regulation was demonstrated. Parent-proximal ratings often look better than probably blinded ratings, which is exactly why the literature remains contested.

evidence.notes: Neurofeedback for Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

effect_quant.comparator: neurofeedback versus control on probably blinded ADHD total symptom ratings at first post-intervention assessment

evidence.citation: CorteseS et al 2016 J Am Acad Child Adolesc Psychiatry
evidence.notes: Neurofeedback for Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder: Meta-Analysis of Clinical and Neuropsychological Outcomes From Randomized Controlled Trials.

effect_quant.comparator: neurofeedback versus control on the least blinded ADHD total symptom ratings; effects were not significant on probably blinded ratings

evidence.citation: HuangX et al 2025 Appl Neuropsychol Child
evidence.notes: Efficacy of portable EEG-based neurofeedback for ADHD: A meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.

effect_quant.comparator: portable EEG-based neurofeedback produced greater reductions in ADHD symptom severity than control conditions in 10 randomized trials
